**Byte mode** — phase 9.
Described by `907`.

## What it publishes

| symbol | unit | kind | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_phase_byte` | 1 | given | 8 | bits sharing one conductor, and therefore pulses per pane |
| `p_bump_byte` | um | given | 32 um | microbump pitch this grade uses. Thirty is a quarter of a micron finer than the conductor count actually permits in the fine zone available |
| `a_mux_lane` | um^2 | measured | 260 um^2 | area of one eight-way multiplexer and its phase logic |
| `n_rework_byte` | 1 | given | 2 | rework attempts a microbump attach permits |
| `n_cond_byte` | 1 | derived | 2.09715e+06 | conductors this grade needs |
| `p_byte_need` | um | derived | 30.2577 um | the pitch that many conductors actually require in the fine zone |
| `a_cond_byte` | um^2 | derived | 1024 um^2 | area one conductor has at the chosen pitch |
| `f_mux_area` | 1 | derived | 0.253906 | how much of it the multiplexer uses |
| `t_pane_byte` | s | derived | 8e-09 s | time for one pane in this grade |
| `t_core_out_y` | s | derived | 0.00027445 s | whole-core transfer time |
| `t_skew_phase` | ps | derived | 1 ps | skew budget within one pulse, which is the hidden cost |
| `ratio_net_y` | 1 | derived | 5242.88 | how much faster than a network interface this grade still is |
| `E_pane_byte` | J | derived | 1.67772e-07 J | energy per pane, unchanged: the same bits cross the same bonds, just not at the same moment |
| `t_skew_min` | ps | given | 0.8 ps | the least skew any distribution can be held to at this scale, from the process |

## What it consumes

| symbol | from | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A_fine` | `056` | 2304 mm^2 | area of the fine zone |
| `E_pane` | `062` | 1.67772e-07 J | energy of one pane transfer |
| `b1` | `046` | 1 bit | one bit. A width carries the unit so that a format's size can be added to a capacity; an exponent needs a pure number. Dividing by this is how a width becomes a count, and it is the only place in the project where a unit quantity is declared for that purpose |
| `f_gnd_ratio` | `063` | 0.2 | share of positions given to power, ground, shielding and strobes, from 064's switching analysis |
| `f_spout_burst` | `062` | 1 GHz | rate a pane transfer runs at during a burst |
| `n_pane_bit` | `062` | 1.67772e+07 bit | the pane, rounded down to a power of two so that its window aligns naturally in 038. It carries the unit because it is a quantity of bits rather than a count of things, and everything downstream of it is a size or a rate |
| `n_pane_core` | `062` | 34306.2 | panes needed to move the whole core |
| `n_rework` | `066` | 0 | rework attempts available. There are none: this is the last operation and both objects are finished |
| `t_core_net` | `062` | 1.43891 s | time to move the whole core over a fast network interface, for the comparison |
| `t_skew_intra` | `065` | 8 ps | skew budget within one tile |

## What it asserts

| tag | relation | because |
|---|---|---|
| `C-068-1` | `n_cond_byte * n_phase_byte ~= n_pane_bit / b1` | the conductors times the phases must be the pane exactly |
| `C-068-2` | `p_bump_byte >= p_byte_need` | the chosen microbump pitch must be no finer than what the conductor count requires in the fine zone available |
| `C-068-3` | `f_mux_area < 0.5` | the multiplexer must fit in under half the pitch, which it comfortably does -- this grade has forty times the area per conductor that 064 has |
| `C-068-4` | `t_skew_phase >= t_skew_min` | the skew budget within one pulse must still be achievable. It is eight times tighter than the bonded grade's for the same nominal rate, and this is the constraint that would fail first if the rate were raised |
| `C-068-5` | `ratio_net_y > 1000` | it must still be three orders of magnitude faster than a network interface, which is what makes eight edges an acceptable price |
| `C-068-6` | `n_rework_byte > n_rework` | this grade must permit rework where the bonded one does not, which is the whole argument for it |
